A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that a T cell receptor that is commonly found in the T cell repertoire of mice immunized with peptide mimotopes is more effective at identifying protective peptides than a T cell receptor with high affinity for the tumor peptide antigen.
we have identified a dominant T cell clone that is frequently present in the tumor and in the immune repertoire elicited by vaccination.
the use of peptide mimics of antigens to elicit immunity against cancer has a long history and continues to be a promising approach for cancer immunotherapy and vaccination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dominant fraction of the tumor-specific T cell repertoire is more important than the high affinity fraction for generating effective mimotope vaccines.
the T cell repertoire that is available to be activated by a vaccine must be considered.
the prevalence of T cell receptors (TCRs) that recognize a tumor antigen should be considered when designing mimotope vaccines for targeted immunotherapy.
